subtype: Approach: dropping the routine when exams come [Revision]
passage: Note, Friday, from Vikas, art teacher. Chitra came after class to say her exams start in three weeks and she wants to cut painting to Sundays only. I expected to hear she was quitting. Her voice was steady, but her hands were tight around her sketchbook. "Only until the exams finish," she said. "Then I will be back at full pace." Her friend Chetan, waiting at the door, asked if she would still join the December show. She said yes. I told Chitra this is a sensible change and not a giving up, and I reserved her wall space and her Sunday easel. Whatever the marks turn out to be, the brush has not been put away.

qa.q: On which day did Chitra plan to keep painting during exams?
qa.a: Chitra planned to keep painting on Sundays.

qa.q: What was Chitra feeling while she explained her plan, according to Vikas?
qa.a: Anxious but determined, since her voice was steady while her hands were tight around the sketchbook.

qa.q: What could Chitra do if exam stress makes Sundays impossible?
qa.a: Cut down to a short sketch or pause with a set return date, because it keeps a link with the hobby.

qa.q: How does Vikas see the change?
qa.a: As a sensible adaptation and not giving up, which is why Vikas reserved her wall space and easel.

grounding: A girl reduces painting to Sundays for exams, planning to return afterwards, adapting the routine instead of quitting.

subtype: Approach: dropping the routine when exams come [Revision]
passage:
Monday
Exams start in three weeks and I haven't finished revising even one Science chapter. Every evening I've been painting for an hour and then panicking at bedtime. Today Vishal Bhaiya found me close to tears over my half-done sunflower and said, "Don't throw the brushes out. Just shrink it." So I made a new plan. Painting only on Sunday, 4 to 5, as a treat after a week of study. The rest of the time the paint box stays on top of the cupboard. After the last exam, back to every evening. I told Mumma. She said, "Good thinking, beti." The sunflower can wait six days for its petals.
Jaya

qa.q: When will Jaya paint during the exams?
What was Jaya feeling before she made the new plan?
qa.a: She was anxious and panicky at bedtime because an hour of painting every evening was crowding out her Science revision 😰.

qa.q: What else could Jaya try if even Sundays start to feel guilty?
qa.a: She could make the Sunday hour shorter or tie it to finishing that week's revision list, adjusting again rather than dropping painting.

qa.q: How might Vishal Bhaiya see Jaya's new plan?
qa.a: He is probably relieved that she shrank painting instead of giving it up, since that was exactly his advice.

grounding: A girl's diary shows her cutting painting to Sundays during exams and planning to return to it afterwards.

subtype: Approach: dropping the routine when exams come [Revision]
passage: Most afternoons after school, Aditi painted clay diyas with Neelam on the veranda of Neelam's house at the edge of the village, often until the light went. Then the half-yearly timetable was pinned up at school: first paper in two weeks. That evening Aditi sat with her maths book open and a diya in her hand, painting instead of reading. She looked at the book, then at the diya. Next morning she told Neelam, "Only Sundays for now. One hour, after my revision. When exams finish I'm back every day." Neelam pouted. "Who'll paint the peacocks?" "Keep them for me." On Sunday they painted six diyas together, and Aditi put the brush down when the hour was up.

qa.q: When was Aditi's first exam paper?
qa.a: Her first paper was in two weeks.

qa.q: What might Aditi have felt, looking from the maths book to the diya?
qa.a: She probably felt torn and a bit guilty, loving the painting but knowing the exams mattered more right now.

qa.q: Which approach suits Aditi better than quitting painting completely, and why?
qa.a: Keeping one Sunday hour after revision, as she did, because she keeps the joy and the skill going while the exams get most of her time.

qa.q: How does Neelam feel about the new plan?
qa.a: Neelam is disappointed and pouts about the peacocks, but still paints with Aditi on Sunday, so the friendship carries on.

grounding: Shows a girl shrinking her painting to Sundays during exams and promising to return, rather than quitting.
